stories.title: Show HN: Cerulion – ROS 2-compatible robotics runtime with multi-process replay
summary: These fast multi-process graphs can then be resimmed deterministically, and existing ROS2 nodes/launch files can run unmodified alongside native Cerulion Rust/Python code.

Installation and quickstart (with a one-shot prompt for your favorite coding agent) here at the repo README: https://github.com/cerulion-inc/cerulionI worked on off-road autonomy during my PhD at MIT, and we kept running into inter-process latency in ROS (2 lidars and 6 cameras).

Wall-clock reads and runtime thread spawns in user code rejected at compile time by macros.ROS 2 is supported with rmw_cerulion for Foxy, Humble, Jazzy and Lyrical, that lets you run ROS2 nodes/launch files unmodified in the same graph as native Cerulion nodes.

stories.title: Distributed Ray Tracer
summary: By distributing the rendering across many different nodes, orchestrated using Hatchet, it makes it possible to render quite high fidelity scenes fairly quickly.

All of this would be possible on a single machine, but would be much slower without dedicated hardware (RT cores, etc).The renderer itself is using well-known ray tracing techniques, with no special considerations there.
The renderer is a slightly modified version of https://github.com/ekzhang/rpt, with additional support for SDF scripting using https://docs.rs/fidget/latest/fidget/.

stories.title: Show HN: Kapso – Iterative learning from enterprise data
summary: We’re now focusing on building AI systems for enterprise data.

Today, we're open-sourcing Kapso (https://github.com/Leeroo-AI/kapso), an engine that runs experiments, deploys the best solution, and learns from every run.The nature of data work is iterative: investigate, form hypotheses, experiment, and improve based on what you learn.
Whether you’re optimizing a warehouse, building a lakehouse pipeline or predicting churn, you need to run experiments and learn what works best in that environment.
